answer: Each new key posts a copper bond of 80 units that unlocks only after 20 clean epochs. The protocol cuts a unique walnut seal from the key address and epoch seed; that seal cannot transfer. Every epoch a random peer runs a basalt check that recomputes the seal and confirms escrow within 5 seconds. Mismatch burns the 80 units and freezes the key for 25 epochs. One honest operator pays once. An attacker forging 1,000 aliases must lock 80,000 units with a fresh walnut seal each, so cost grows with no pooling.
